title: Creating and deleting files and folders
lead: Use mkdir, touch, rmdir and rm to build and clean up a file structure in a safe practice area.
objectives: You create folders and nested structures with mkdir and mkdir -p.
You create empty files with touch, several at once using brace expansion.
You know the difference between rmdir and rm -r and check before deleting.

sections.title: Creating: mkdir and touch
body: First make a safe **practice area**: a folder `practice` in your home directory. Mistakes then only affect it. As a normal user you cannot write to system directories like `/etc` — that is a protection mechanism.
`mkdir` creates folders, `touch` creates empty files. Brace expansion produces several names: `touch {a,b,c}.txt` creates `a.txt b.txt c.txt`.

commands.where: For projects, backups or practice areas.

commands.what: Also creates missing parent folders; no error if the folder exists.
commands.why: One command builds the whole tree.

commands.what: Creates an empty file or updates an existing file's timestamp.
commands.where: When you quickly need an empty file.
commands.why: A starting point for scripts and test files.
You see what will be affected before deleting or moving.

sections.tip: Always verify the result with ls after an action.

sections.title: Deleting: rm and rmdir
body: Linux has **no trash can** on the command line: files removed with `rm` are gone. So check with `ls` what you are about to delete.

`rmdir` removes only **empty** folders; for a non-empty one it fails and protects you. To delete a folder with its contents you need `rm -r`. Using `rm` on a folder without `-r` gives 'Is a directory'. In this simulator dangerous commands such as `rm -rf /` are refused.

commands.why: For space and tidiness — but use with care.
Stops you from accidentally deleting a full folder.

commands.what: Deletes a folder together with its contents.
commands.why: Clears the tree in one command; use after checking.

sections.tip: Make it a habit: first `ls -R folder`, then `rm -r folder`.
sections.warn: Before pressing ENTER, re-read which folder `rm -r` will delete. In the wrong directory it destroys your whole project.
sections.danger: On a real system never type `rm -rf /` or `rm -rf ~`. It causes irreversible data loss; only the simulator refuses it here.

t01.text: In your home directory create a practice folder with `mkdir practice`.
t01.hint: Make sure you are home first with `cd ~`.

t02.hint: The directory in the prompt changes.

t03.text: Create an empty file with `touch file1.txt`.

t04.hint: In ls -l the line starts with d.

t05.text: Build the nested structure in one command with `mkdir -p project/src/code`.

t06.text: List the structure with its subfolders using `ls -R project`.

t07.text: Create three files in one command with `touch {a,b,c}.txt`.
t07.hint: Separate with commas inside the braces, no spaces.

t08.text: Create `delete_me.txt` with `touch`, then delete it with `rm`.
t08.hint: Two commands; check with ls that it is gone.

t09.text: Try to delete the non-empty folder with `rmdir project`. Did it fail? Why?

t10.text: Delete the folder with its contents using `rm -r project`.
t10.hint: Look inside first with ls -R proje.

t11.text: Run `rm folder1` on the folder without `-r` and read the error.

t12.text: Challenge: `mkdir -p ~/practice/final_project`, `touch report.txt` inside it, `ls -R final_project` one level up, then `rm -r final_project`.
t12.hint: To create the file, `cd ~/practice/final_project` first, then leave with `cd ..`.

t13.text: As a normal user, try to create a folder in a system directory: `mkdir /etc/practice`. What happens?
t13.hint: Expect Permission denied; system directories are protected.

t14.text: Debug: the folder `~/old_project` cannot be removed (`rmdir` fails). Remove it together with its contents.
t14.hint: It contains files; `rmdir` is not enough, you need `rm -r`.

t15.text: Mini project: under `~/web` create the folders `css`, `js`, `img` with a single `mkdir -p` and the file `index.html` with `touch`.

t16.text: TICKET #2310 — Accounting expects `jan.txt`, `feb.txt`, `mar.txt` in `~/archive/2026/q1`. Build the structure.
t16.hint: `mkdir -p` for the folders, `touch` with brace for the files.

q1.q: What is true for a file deleted with `rm`?
q1.explain: The command line has no trash can; deletion is permanent.

q2.explain: -p (parents) builds the whole path at once and does not complain if the folder already exists.

q3.q: What happens if you run `rmdir` on a non-empty folder?
options: It fails and the folder stays
The folder is deleted with its contents
q3.explain: rmdir only removes empty folders. For non-empty ones use `rm -r`.

q4.q: Which command is most commonly used to create an empty file?
q4.explain: `touch file` creates an empty file or updates its timestamp.

summary: `mkdir` creates folders, `mkdir -p` nested folders, `touch` empty files.
`touch {a,b,c}.txt` uses brace expansion to create several files.
`rmdir` removes only empty folders, `rm -r` non-empty ones; there is no trash.
Check with `ls` before and after every action.

glossary.meaning: A structure that holds files; the same concept.
An operation that includes subfolders; -r or -R.
The shell turns patterns like {a,b,c} into several words.
The time a file was last modified.

vm.intro: On your VM, first create a safe practice folder; never try `rm -r` where real data lives.

v01.title: Build a project tree
v01.text: Build a nested structure in the practice folder and paste the `ls -R` output.
differs: The order of `ls -R` may differ; `src` and `test` must appear.
Empty folders are separated by a blank line in `ls -R` output.

v02.title: See the protection
v02.text: As a normal user try to create a folder in a system directory and paste the error.

blocks.expected: mkdir: cannot create directory ‘/etc/practice’: Permission denied

differs: On a localised system the message may be translated.
If the folder was created you are root; use a normal user and remove it with `sudo rmdir /etc/practice`.

v03.title: Clean up
v03.text: Look inside first, then delete the practice folder. If no errors, press "Done".

blocks.expected: ls: cannot access '/home/student/practice': No such file or directory

differs: If you see `rm: cannot remove ... Is a directory`, you forgot `-r`.
